lines.en: What history teaches us is that those who refuse to change are the first to be left behind.
It is often said that the only constant in life is change itself.
Not until the factory closed did the town realize how much it had depended on it.
However painful a change may be at first, it often opens doors we never knew existed.
Were the old market to disappear, the neighborhood would lose more than shops; it would lose its memory.
My grandfather is said to have resisted smartphones for years, and now he video-calls us every day.
It is not the change itself that frightens people, but the fear of losing what they know.
Little by little, the village adapted, and what was once strange became part of daily life.
What survivors of any crisis share is not strength, but the willingness to adapt.
Rarely does life ask our permission before it changes; it simply changes, and we must follow.
What the pandemic proved was that even the oldest institutions can change overnight when they must.
It is not the fastest company that survives, but the one most willing to question its own success.
So quickly is technology changing that the job my daughter will do has not even been invented yet.
Were we to resist every new idea, we would still be living as people did a thousand years ago.
It is said that the best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago, and the second best time is now.
